sections.title: Shifting from Departments to Processes
sections.text:
must shift from thinking in “departments” to thinking in “processes.” SAP itself
presents SAP S/4HANA in terms of integrated processes such as procure-to-pay,
order-to-cash, and record-to-report, not just modules or transaction codes. This
chapter builds that process mindset.

Chapter 2 - From Functions to Business
Processes

sections.title: What is a Business Process?
sections.text:
A business process is a repeatable sequence of activities that takes an input,
applies work to it, and produces a meaningful business outcome.
Key characteristics of a process:

For example, “Pay a vendor” is not just a finance task. It is the final step of a
broader process that started when someone requested a purchase, continued
when an order was placed and goods arrived, and completed when the vendor
was paid and the liability cleared.
It usually starts with a
trigger (a need, a
request, an event).
It passes through
multiple steps, often
crossing departments.
It ends with a clear
outcome (goods
delivered, cash
collected, vendor paid,
report produced).
It can be measured
and improved (time,
cost, quality,
compliance).

sections.title: Functions vs Processes: Why the difference matters
sections.text:
ERP systems like SAP S/4HANA are designed around such processes. SAP
describes SAP S/4HANA as supporting end-to-end business operations across
finance, supply chain, sales, and other areas in one integrated system, which
makes process thinking essential for consultants.
A function is a responsibility area or department, such as “Procurement” or
“Finance.”
A process is the end-to-end journey a transaction follows through several
functions.
Compare these two views:
Functional view of buying:
“Procurement buys material, warehouse receives it, finance pays for it.”
Process view of buying:
“A user raises a requirement → it is approved → a purchase order is
created → goods are received and recorded → the vendor invoice is
checked → payment is made → accounting entries are posted.”
The functional view is siloed; the process view is integrated.

SAP S/4HANA is built on the process view. For example, SAP does not only say
“there is a Materials Management module.” SAP explicitly talks about procure-to-
pay as a supported process, linking sourcing, purchasing, inventory, and financial
settlement in one flow. Similarly, SAP highlights order-to-cash and record-to-
report as end-to-end processes supported in SAP S/4HANA Cloud.
For an aspiring functional consultant, this means:

You cannot stop at “I know
MM” or “I know FI.”
You must be able to
explain how processes
move across MM, SD, FI,
and other areas.
You must see where your
module fits in the larger
process story.

sections.title: The Procure‑to‑Pay (P2P) Story
sections.text:
Business scenario
Imagine a manufacturing company that needs raw materials to produce
finished goods. The P2P process covers everything from identifying that need
to paying the supplier and recording the final accounting impact.
SAP positions sourcing and procurement as an end-to-end capability in SAP
S/4HANA, connecting suppliers, purchasing, inventory, and finance within one
system.
Typical P2P steps (conceptual)

Identify need
Create Purchase Requisition (PR)
Send PO to vendor
Vendor Invoice Vendor Payment
Goods Receipt (GR)
Create Purchase Order (PO)
Approve the requisition

Identify need
A department realizes that a material or service is required (for production,
maintenance, office use, etc.).
Create Purchase Requisition (PR)
An internal document is created to request the purchase of a specific material
or service in a required quantity and timeframe.
Approve the requisition
Depending on the company’s approval matrix, managers or budget owners
approve the PR.
Create Purchase Order (PO)
Procurement converts the approved PR into a PO or creates a PO directly,
selecting a vendor, defining price, quantity, and delivery terms.
Send PO to vendor
The PO is shared with the vendor as a formal commercial commitment.

Goods Receipt (GR)
When goods arrive, the warehouse or receiving team checks quantity and
quality, and records a goods receipt in the system.
Vendor Invoice
The vendor sends an invoice for the supplied goods or services. The invoice is
matched against the PO and GR (three-way match concept).
Vendor Payment
After verification and approval, payment is issued to the vendor, and the
liability is cleared in finance.

sections.title: Cross-functional nature of P2P
sections.text:
The user / requesting department initiates the need.
Procurement manages vendor selection and PO creation.
Warehouse/stores handle goods receipt and inventory updates.
Finance handles invoice verification and payment.
In SAP S/4HANA, this process connects MM (Materials Management), FI (Financial
Accounting), and sometimes other areas, all operating on shared master data and
integrated transactions.
For consultants, understanding the P2P conceptually is crucial before mapping
each step to SAP documents or configuration.

sections.title: The Order‑to‑Cash (O2C) Story
sections.text:
Business scenario
Now consider the sales side: a customer wants to buy a product or service. The
O2C process starts when the customer expresses interest and ends when
payment is received and recorded.
SAP explicitly lists order-to-cash as one of the core business processes supported
in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, emphasizing its role in connecting sales, fulfillment, billing,
and finance.

Typical O2C steps (Conceptual)

Customer inquiry or quotation
Sales Order (SO) creation
Availability check and delivery
planning
Delivery and goods issue
Billing / invoicing
Incoming payment

Customer inquiry or quotation
The customer asks for information or a quote. The sales team may issue a
quotation with pricing and terms.
Sales Order (SO) creation
Once the customer confirms, a sales order is created, capturing products,
quantities, prices, delivery dates, and terms.
Availability check and delivery planning
The system checks stock availability or triggers production planning as
needed. Delivery is scheduled.
Delivery and goods issue
Warehouse picks and packs goods, and a goods issue is posted, reducing
inventory and signaling that goods are now with the customer or in transit.
Billing/Invoicing
Based on the deliveries, an invoice is created and sent to the customer.
Incoming Payment
The customer pays as per the agreed terms. Finance posts the incoming
payment and clears the open receivable.

Cross-functional nature of O2C

In SAP S/4HANA, the O2C process spans SD (Sales and Distribution), MM (for
inventory aspects), and FI (for financial postings), again leveraging integrated
master data and process flows.
Sales manages customer interaction,
quotations, and orders.
Warehouse / logistics handle physical goods
movement.
Customer service may be involved in
coordination and communication.
Finance manages billing, receivables, and
incoming payments.

sections.title: The Record‑to‑Report (R2R) Story
sections.text:
Business scenario
Record-to-report covers how financial information is captured, consolidated, and
presented to stakeholders. It is the link between daily operations and the financial
statements that management, investors, and regulators rely on.
SAP’s finance capabilities in SAP S/4HANA are described as supporting record-to-
report, from transactional postings through period-end closing and reporting.

Typical R2R steps

Daily recording of transactions
Sub-ledger and general ledger updates
Reconciliations
Adjustments and accruals
Period close
Financial reporting
Analysis and decisions

Typical R2R steps
Daily recording of transactions
Operational events (purchases, sales, payroll, expenses, asset activities) create
accounting entries.
Sub-ledger and general ledger updates
Sub-ledgers (such as accounts payable, accounts receivable, and assets) feed
into the general ledger.
Reconciliations
Accounts are reconciled to ensure balances are accurate and consistent (bank
reconciliation, intercompany reconciliation, etc.).
Adjustments and accruals
Period-end adjustments are made for items like accruals, prepayments, and
provisions.
Period close
The period is closed for postings, ensuring data stability for reporting.

Financial reporting
Financial statements and management reports are produced: balance sheet,
income statement, cash flow, and internal performance views.
Analysis and decisions
Management reviews results, identifies trends, and makes decisions for the
next period.

Why R2R depends on P2P and O2C
R2R does not exist in isolation. Its accuracy depends on:

SAP S/4HANA uses a simplified data model and integrated posting logic so that
operational processes feed finance in real time, supporting faster and more
reliable record-to-report cycles.
How cleanly P2P transactions are recorded (correct
vendor, amount, account).
How accurately O2C transactions are captured (correct
customer, revenue, tax).
How completely other processes (payroll, assets,
projects) are integrated.

sections.title: Process Thinking vs “Button-click” Thinking
sections.text:
Many new learners approach SAP as a set of screens and codes: “Which
transaction creates a PO?” or “Which app shows customer balances?” That
approach leads to shallow understanding and interview difficulty.
Process thinking looks like this:

SAP itself structures its learning journeys and cloud ERP descriptions around end-
to-end business processes and line-of-business functions rather than only
technical transactions. For an aspiring functional consultant, thinking in P2P,
O2C, and R2R terms is non-negotiable.
“What triggers this process?”
“What are the key steps end to end?”
“Who owns each step?”
“What documents are created?”
“What is the financial or inventory impact?”
“What happens upstream and downstream if something changes?”

sections.title: Simple Cross-process Example: How Everything Connects
sections.text:
Consider a full cycle that touches all three processes:
Simple Cross-process Example: How Everything

If any step in P2P or O2C is incorrect (wrong quantities, wrong prices, wrong
accounts), the R2R process produces misleading financial statements. This is why
SAP S/4HANA emphasizes integrated, real-time transaction and analytics in one
environment, leveraging SAP HANA and embedded analytics capabilities.
The company buys raw materials through
P2P.
The finished goods are sold through O2C.
Those materials are used in production to
create finished goods.
All purchasing and sales activities are
recorded and summarized in R2R.
